title: Normalize tenant resolution across proxy chains and API-key rotation flows
creator: Maya R. Thompson
description: Observed sporadic misattribution of token/usage to parent org when requests traverse multiple proxies and API-key rotation occurs mid-flight. Root cause appears to be non-deterministic tenant resolution order combined with a short-lived cache eviction during rotation (proxy attaches temporary delegation header, backend uses cached mapping for 'owner' that races with rotation job). Impact: incorrect billing for a small percentage of requests (0.03-0.2% of traffic during rotation windows), skewed per-project quotas, and occasional customer-facing quota errors despite sufficient allowance. This ticket standardizes the canonical tenant resolution algorithm, hardens caches against rotation races, and instruments a safe backfill for historical misattributed usage
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two projects A (parent) and B (child) with separate API keys and quotas
2) Start request stream through Proxy-Chain: client -> edge-proxy -> tenant-proxy (adds delegated token header) -> router -> inference runtime
3) Trigger API-key rotation for project B while requests are in flight (rotation job updates tenant mapping and invalidates cache TTL to 0)
4) Observe that some requests are attributed to project A or root org in billing metrics and that rate limiter counters decrement for the wrong tenant
investigation_log: 2026-03-03: Pager alert from billing-ops; spike in cross-project attribution correlated with scheduled rotation job for a large enterprise customer
2026-03-04: Gathered traces; found tenant-resolution decision recorded at both edge and runtime with conflicting values in ~0.06% samples
2026-03-05: Added debug logs to router and proxy showing header precedence and cache TTL during rotation window
2026-03-06: Replayed captured traffic in staging with forced cache eviction; reproduced misattribution deterministically at lower QPS
2026-03-09: Verified that rate-limiter counters are updated based on the first-seen tenant tag; downstream billing job re-hydrates attribution from token metadata which was stale
root_cause_summary: Combined factors: (a) inconsistent tenant precedence rules between edge and runtime (edge favored delegated header, runtime favored cached owner), (b) cache invalidation set to immediate during rotation, causing transient absence of canonical mapping, and (c) billing backfill path relied on token->owner join that could choose a fallback parent org when owner was transiently missing
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce a deterministic tenant-resolution layer (canonical_resolution) invoked at router entry that stamps a signed tenant-assertion header; 2) Make tenant cache invalidation coordinated: rotation emits a grace TTL (e.g., 60s) and rotation-phase flag so in-flight requests use last-known-good mapping instead of falling back; 3) Update billing backfill join to prefer the canonical_resolution audit log before falling back to legacy token mapping
implementation_tasks: A. Add canonical_resolution service and gRPC endpoint (router -> canonical_resolution) with signed assertion payload
B. Modify proxies (edge-proxy, tenant-proxy) to respect and forward signed assertions; add validation at runtime
C. Change rotation job to set grace TTL + rotation-phase metadata and publish to rotation-utility topic
D. Update rate-limiter to use canonical assertion for counter attribution (atomic increment API that requires signed tenant id)
E. Add feature-flag 'tenant-canonical' for staged rollout and safe rollback
F. Create a backfill consumer to re-process confirmed misattributed intervals using canonical_resolution audit log
migration_plan: 1) Deploy canonical_resolution behind feature flag in staging and run synthetic traffic through multi-proxy paths
2) Deploy proxy + runtime validation in Canary mode to 10% of traffic for 48h; monitor attribution delta and rate-limiter errors
3) Run incremental backfill job scoped to last 7 days of rotations for affected customers; validate cost reconciliation in billing sandbox
4) Gradually expand feature flag to 50% then 100% after 72h stable telemetry
5) Final step: retire legacy fallback join after 30 days and mark rotation fixes as completed
rollout_and_monitoring: Metrics to watch: misattribution_rate (should drop to <1e-4), per-tenant quota mismatch alerts, rate_limiter_error_rate
SLOs: no customer-facing quota denials attributable to rotation after Canary; rollback if misattribution_rate increases or user complaints rise
Post-deploy check: run reconciliation job to compare old vs new attribution on a sampled window
backfill_strategy: Write idempotent re-attribution consumer that reads raw request logs + rotation audit stream and emits corrected billing deltas into billing_corrections topic
Process only windows where rotation jobs touched tenant mapping (to limit scope)
Emit a summarized reconciliation report and apply customer-visible billing credits only after finance signoff
Keep per-request annotations in historic logs (tenant_assertion_v1) for 90 days
risks: Signed assertion introduces crypto overhead and requires key management; mitigate by short-lived HMAC keys rotated daily
Backfill may produce billing churn; coordinate with finance and CS before applying credits
Feature-flag complexity could lead to dual-path attribution if proxies and runtime drift; plan explicit interop tests
Increased latency at router (one extra canonical_resolution call) — mitigate with local caching and 100ms P95 target
